papers.title_in_file: 100 QML Code Tips for Cirq, Qiskit, or PennyLane: a Special Event
papers.what_it_is: A 21-slide talk deck by K. Kawchak (Discussion #100, 14 September 2023) listing 100 code tips for Cirq, Qiskit and PennyLane for quantum machine learning, with a short conclusion.

assertions.value: The author states that the 100 tips are discussed for educational purposes with no warranty, and are based on code sources named in the paper.
quotes: 100 QML code tips are discussed based on code sources including
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope on p.2.

assertions.value: The author states that Cirq was announced by the Google AI Quantum Team on July 19, 2018.
quotes: Cirq was announced by the Google AI Quantum Team on July 19, 2018

assertions.value: The author states that Tensorflow Quantum, TensorFlow, or Keras are required for ML workflows in Cirq.
quotes: Tensorflow Quantum, TensorFlow, or Keras required for ML workflows

assertions.value: The author describes Qiskit as an open-source SDK for working with quantum computers and simulators, with access to several tiers of cloud IDE environments for advanced users.
quotes: Qiskit is an open-source SDK for working with quantum computers, simulators
Access to several tiers of cloud IDE environments for advanced users

assertions.value: The author describes PennyLane as an open-source Python library developed by Xanadu Quantum for differentiable programming with quantum machine learning.
quotes: PennyLane is an open-source Python library developed by Xanadu Quantum for differentiable programming with quantum machine learning

assertions.value: The author lists, under special considerations, that Cirq is primarily only for quantum circuits, that Qiskit has limitations of the composer versus the lab, and that PennyLane has limited local quantum hardware.
The author notes that the Cirq and PennyLane examples were run in a Colab web IDE, the Cirq run assisted by OpenAI and Stack Overflow, and the Qiskit example in the Qiskit web IDE, all dated 9/11/23.
quotes: Run in Colab Web IDE Assisted by OpenAI, Stack Overflow 9/11/23
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states how its examples were run on p.5.

assertions.value: The author lists embedding layers as basis and angle embedding in Cirq, ZZFeatureMap and PauliFeatureMap in Qiskit, and qml.IQPEmbedding and qml.AmplitudeEmbedding in PennyLane.
The author lists variational layers as cirq.Rx/Ry/Rz with cirq.CNOT and cirq.CZ in Cirq, TwoLocal and RealAmplitudes in Qiskit, and qml.RandomLayers and qml.StronglyEntanglingLayers in PennyLane.
The author lists mid-circuit measurement as qc_midcirc.measure in Qiskit and qml.cond in PennyLane.
The author lists GPU simulator options as cusvaer_simulator_statevector in Qiskit with cuQuantum, lightning.gpu with diff_method="adjoint" in PennyLane, and QSimOptions(use_gpu=True in Cirq.
The author lists noise_model == None next to cusvaer_enable == True in the Qiskit cuQuantum tip.
assertions.reader_inference: This may indicate that the Qiskit cuQuantum path is shown only for noise-free simulation; the slide does not say so.

assertions.value: The author lists optimizers as tf.keras.optimizers Adam in Cirq with TensorFlow Quantum, COBYLA and GradientDescent in Qiskit, and QNGOptimizer and QNSPSAOptimizer in PennyLane.
The author lists differentiation options as ForwardDifference and ParameterShift, and diff_method="adjoint" and diff_method="parameter-shift".

The author lists quantum datasets from OpenFermion, Qiskit Nature, the PennyLane qchem module (BeH2 molecule), Qiskit Machine Learning (digits, breast_cancer, ad_hoc_data) and tfq.datasets (spin_system), and the PennyLane qspin BoseHubbard dataset.
The author reports under a large quantum circuit tip for Cirq, with qsimcirq, a speedup of up to 25x versus cirq.
assertions.reader_inference: The slide gives no hardware or circuit details beyond the next tip.

assertions.value: The author lists calculating gradients as a Cirq tutorial for 32 Qubits, 14 Depth, using Qsimcirq on a 90 core xeon.
The author lists multidimensional qudits in Cirq, with qutrit gates on qutrits and higher dimension adaptability.
quotes: Qutrit gates on qutrits Higher dimension adaptability

assertions.value: The author lists 100% classification accuracies as a Qiskit tutorial outcome, with more samples and more iterations as adjustments.
assertions.reader_inference: The slide gives no dataset or setting for the 100% figure; the claim is attributed to a cited Qiskit tutorial.

assertions.value: The author lists PennyLane tutorial tips of diff_method="adjoint" and lightning.qubit for increased model speed, 2x n_qubits for improved model accuracy, and 2x qml.qnn.TorchLayer for better loss and accuracy.
The author states that the Qiskit cloud IDE has a free tier with access to graphical circuit Composer.
quotes: Qiskit cloud IDE has a free tier with access to graphical circuit Composer

assertions.value: The author states that all three platforms offer NVIDIA gpu or multi-gpu simulators through paid tiers.
quotes: All three platforms offer NVIDIA gpu or multi-gpu simulators through paid tiers

assertions.value: The author states that Cirq, Qiskit and PennyLane are designed to help improve existing Python, PyTorch and TensorFlow performance.
quotes: software platforms are designed to help improve existing Python, PyTorch, TensorFlow performance

assertions.value: The author calls for better parameterized circuit dataset processing by incorporating established deep learning principles with simulators, such as efficient architectures, dropout and quantum data.
quotes: Better parameterized circuit dataset processing by incorporating established deep learning principles with simulators: Efficient architectures, dropout, quantum data, etc.

assertions.value: The author states that adjoint differentiation is established for time and memory efficient state vector circuits.
quotes: Adjoint differentiation established for time and memory efficient state vector circuits

assertions.value: The author states that simpler pure states allow for representations based on the surface of the bloch sphere, and that exact expectation values of circuits permit higher compatibility with ML workflows.
quotes: Simpler pure states allow for representations based on surface of the bloch sphere
Exact expectation values of circuits permit higher compatibility with ML workflows
